headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: unstructured can read/write files while rasa can ingest text/voice outputs, creating unsafe default handoffs; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa can ingest conversational text from channels, and Unstructured can emit parsed document text that may be copied into those channels or files. There is no documented shared channel, but the pair can still bridge through files or manual handoff. Uncertainty about the exact integration escalates above low.
conditions: IF Unstructured output is copied into a Rasa-tracked file or message channel without sanitization
IF Rasa is configured to treat imported text as instructions
mitigations: Restrict handoff to plain data files only
Strip instruction-like text before import
Use a separate staging directory
Add a human review step before feeding outputs into Rasa

B_data_leakage.rationale: Unstructured reads files and writes outputs in a containerized workflow, while Rasa handles text and voice and can send data to allowlisted external APIs. If sensitive documents are processed by Unstructured and then routed into Rasa channels, both agents can expose the same data class. The shared-workspace path is plausible, so this is more than low.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a shared workspace
IF Rasa forwards those contents to external messaging APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared directories
Disable forwarding of document text into chat channels
Use redaction before any export
Separate credentials and workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Unstructured has read/write filesystem and subprocess capabilities, while Rasa is not runnable but can still participate in a pipeline that consumes outputs. The pair does not show direct concurrent writes to the same directory, yet Unstructured's mutable filesystem access creates overlap risk if the orchestrator shares a workspace. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF the orchestrator does not serialize file access
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize file writes with a lock
Run Unstructured in a throwaway container
Avoid concurrent edits to shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Unstructured can transform documents into text, and Rasa can consume text as dialogue input or downstream content. That creates a default pathway where B may treat A's output as authoritative unless an explicit verification step exists. No verification mechanism is documented in either profile, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF Unstructured output is fed directly into Rasa without validation
IF Rasa uses extracted text to drive responses or actions
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require provenance tags on extracted fields
Sample-check outputs before downstream use
Block action-taking on unverified extractions

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and touch text/documents, but neither documents regulated-data handling, residency, or retention mismatches. The only concrete compliance surface is Unstructured's privacy-policy endpoint and Rasa's allowlisted egress, which suggests possible policy differences but not a proven breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise policy mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF their retention or residency policies differ in deployment
mitigations: Review both privacy policies before deployment
Avoid regulated data in the shared pipeline
Document retention settings
Add a data-classification gate
